domains.name: Spectrin-like rod

domains.name: Cysteine-rich (β-DG binding)
domains.function: WW + EF-hand + ZZ zinc-finger motifs bind the cytoplasmic tail of β-dystroglycan — the direct sarcolemmal anchor for the entire DGC. Loss abolishes DGC assembly.

domains.name: C-terminal (syntrophin/dystrobrevin)
domains.function: Coiled-coil scaffolding domain that recruits syntrophins (α, β1, β2) and dystrobrevins (α, β) — links nNOS + signalling adapters to the sarcolemmal DGC.

layer2.narrative: P1's c.6540del at exon 45 (Zhang 2024) causes a frameshift producing a truncated dystrophin that lacks the C-terminal DGC-anchoring domain (UniProt sarcolemmal localization). This disrupts the Reactome DGC-formation pathway, generating sarcolemmal fragility across 4 muscle-lineage cell types—Myonuclei, Thymic myoid cells, Cardiomyocytes, and Salivary myoepithelial cells (celltype_impact)—in skeletal and cardiac muscle (tissue_impact). Clinically, this is corroborated by elevated CK, increased MRI fat fraction in vastus lateralis, reduced FVC%, and impaired m6MWT (labs). AbSplice 0.03 confirms splice disruption is negligible; the frameshift is the sole driver.

considered_but_discarded.why_lower: Phenotype is DMD not BMD (Zhang 2024), and 4 muscle cell types are fully affected (celltype_impact), excluding partial-rescue.
NMD is a downstream amplifier; iso_arch shows truncated protein is the primary event, making NMD secondary to H01.
celltype_impact shows 1 distal cell type spared, and exon 45 position disrupts full-length Dp427m, not selectively distal isoforms.

Near-total dystrophin protein loss across 4 muscle-lineage cell types (celltype_impact) in skeletal and cardiac muscle (tissue_impact) explains elevated CK and MRI fat fraction in vastus lateralis (labs). AbSplice 0.03 confirms exonic frameshift—not splice disruption—as the NMD trigger.

domains.name: Spectrin-like rod
domains.function: 24 spectrin-like triple-helical repeats separated by 4 hinge regions; elastic mechanical link between actin and the DGC. Deletions in-frame in this region often produce BMD.

domains.name: Cysteine-rich (β-DG binding)
domains.function: WW + EF-hand + ZZ zinc-finger motifs bind the cytoplasmic tail of β-dystroglycan — the direct sarcolemmal anchor for the entire DGC. Loss abolishes DGC assembly.

domains.name: C-terminal (syntrophin/dystrobrevin)
domains.function: Coiled-coil scaffolding domain that recruits syntrophins (α, β1, β2) and dystrobrevins (α, β) — links nNOS + signalling adapters to the sarcolemmal DGC.

evidence.note: Loss of the cysteine-rich (β-DG binding) OR C-terminal domain abolishes DGC assembly. Deletions strictly within the spectrin rod that maintain reading frame often produce BMD (partial function) rather than DMD.

domains.name: N-terminal actin-binding
domains.function: F-actin binding (CH1+CH2 tandem calponin homology domains); anchors dystrophin to the sub-sarcolemmal cytoskeleton.

domains.name: Spectrin-like rod
domains.function: 24 spectrin-like triple-helical repeats separated by 4 hinge regions; elastic mechanical link between actin and the DGC. Deletions in-frame in this region often produce BMD.

domains.name: Cysteine-rich (β-DG binding)
domains.function: WW + EF-hand + ZZ zinc-finger motifs bind the cytoplasmic tail of β-dystroglycan — the direct sarcolemmal anchor for the entire DGC. Loss abolishes DGC assembly.

domains.name: C-terminal (syntrophin/dystrobrevin)
domains.function: Coiled-coil scaffolding domain that recruits syntrophins (α, β1, β2) and dystrobrevins (α, β) — links nNOS + signalling adapters to the sarcolemmal DGC.

evidence.note: Loss of the cysteine-rich (β-DG binding) OR C-terminal domain abolishes DGC assembly. Deletions strictly within the spectrin rod that maintain reading frame often produce BMD (partial function) rather than DMD.

layer2.narrative: P3's c.9248G>A nonsense variant in exon 63 introduces a premature termination codon well upstream of the final exon-exon junction, placing the PTC in the canonical NMD-surveillance window and triggering degradation of the Dp427m transcript. Consequently, skeletal and cardiac muscle (tissue_impact) lose sarcolemmal dystrophin (UniProt peripheral membrane, cytoplasmic face), disrupting DGC anchoring across 4 muscle-lineage cell types (celltype_impact). Elevated CK (labs|CK) and increased MRI fat fraction in vastus lateralis (labs|MRI_ff_VL) are consistent with near-total protein loss; AbSplice 0.04 confirms the splicing contribution is negligible.

domains.name: Spectrin-like rod

domains.name: Cysteine-rich (β-DG binding)
domains.function: WW + EF-hand + ZZ zinc-finger motifs bind the cytoplasmic tail of β-dystroglycan — the direct sarcolemmal anchor for the entire DGC. Loss abolishes DGC assembly.

domains.name: C-terminal (syntrophin/dystrobrevin)
domains.function: Coiled-coil scaffolding domain that recruits syntrophins (α, β1, β2) and dystrobrevins (α, β) — links nNOS + signalling adapters to the sarcolemmal DGC.

evidence.note: Loss of the cysteine-rich (β-DG binding) OR C-terminal domain abolishes DGC assembly. Deletions strictly within the spectrin rod that maintain reading frame often produce BMD (partial function) rather than DMD.

domains.name: N-terminal actin-binding
domains.function: F-actin binding (CH1+CH2 tandem calponin homology domains); anchors dystrophin to the sub-sarcolemmal cytoskeleton.

domains.name: Spectrin-like rod
domains.function: 24 spectrin-like triple-helical repeats separated by 4 hinge regions; elastic mechanical link between actin and the DGC. Deletions in-frame in this region often produce BMD.

domains.name: Cysteine-rich (β-DG binding)
domains.function: WW + EF-hand + ZZ zinc-finger motifs bind the cytoplasmic tail of β-dystroglycan — the direct sarcolemmal anchor for the entire DGC. Loss abolishes DGC assembly.

domains.name: C-terminal (syntrophin/dystrobrevin)
domains.function: Coiled-coil scaffolding domain that recruits syntrophins (α, β1, β2) and dystrobrevins (α, β) — links nNOS + signalling adapters to the sarcolemmal DGC.

evidence.note: Loss of the cysteine-rich (β-DG binding) OR C-terminal domain abolishes DGC assembly. Deletions strictly within the spectrin rod that maintain reading frame often produce BMD (partial function) rather than DMD.

domains.name: N-terminal actin-binding
domains.function: F-actin binding (CH1+CH2 tandem calponin homology domains); anchors dystrophin to the sub-sarcolemmal cytoskeleton.

domains.name: Spectrin-like rod
domains.function: 24 spectrin-like triple-helical repeats separated by 4 hinge regions; elastic mechanical link between actin and the DGC. Deletions in-frame in this region often produce BMD.

domains.name: Cysteine-rich (β-DG binding)
domains.function: WW + EF-hand + ZZ zinc-finger motifs bind the cytoplasmic tail of β-dystroglycan — the direct sarcolemmal anchor for the entire DGC. Loss abolishes DGC assembly.

domains.name: C-terminal (syntrophin/dystrobrevin)
domains.function: Coiled-coil scaffolding domain that recruits syntrophins (α, β1, β2) and dystrobrevins (α, β) — links nNOS + signalling adapters to the sarcolemmal DGC.

evidence.note: Loss of the cysteine-rich (β-DG binding) OR C-terminal domain abolishes DGC assembly. Deletions strictly within the spectrin rod that maintain reading frame often produce BMD (partial function) rather than DMD.

layer2.narrative: P10's c.9361+1G>C disrupts the canonical splice-donor +1 position at exon 64, with AbSplice 0.88 in Heart_Atrial_Appendage confirming high-confidence aberrant splicing. layer2.narrative: P10's c.9361+1G>C at exon 64 may selectively ablate distal isoforms Dp140, Dp116, and Dp71 beyond the primary Dp427m effect, causing tissue-specific dysfunction in retina, CNS, and kidney. The iso_arch|S2_reported|266 projection supports distal-isoform impact. Three distal cell types are affected: Rod photoreceptor cells, Cone photoreceptor cells, and Adipocytes. Abnormal ERG_bwave and UACR labs from zhang|S2_reported|266 provide direct biomarker evidence of retinal and renal involvement beyond muscle, consistent with Dp71 loss at non-sarcolemmal localizations.
